title: One Point Lesson - Fouling Trend & Cleaning Schedule (PDT-5605) (OPL-EA-5601-06)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-EA-5601-06 - Fouling Trend & Cleaning Schedule (PDT-5605).

Equipment: EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER), Discipline: Instrument, Area: 5600 - SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: N/A (control loop only), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-5601.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains fouling trend & cleaning schedule (pdt-5605) for EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER) in the SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM. Trending the tube-side differential pressure predicts when cleaning is due before the duty is lost. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: De-energise and isolate the loop; place the function to bypass/inhibit under permit.
- Precaution 2: Inform the panel operator before working on any trip, valve or transmitter.
- Precaution 3: Take care with instrument air / hydraulic pressure when disconnecting tubing.
- Precaution 4: Verify intrinsic-safety / Ex integrity is restored before returning to service.
- Precaution 5: Wear correct PPE and follow ESD/override control procedures.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: HART communicator / positioner software (e.g. ValveLink)
- Tool 2: Loop calibrator & decade box / pressure source
- Tool 3: Digital multimeter and clamp meter
- Tool 4: Span/zero test gas or reference standards
- Tool 5: Torque screwdriver and small hand tools
- Tool 6: Certified test/inhibit permit

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Log PDT-5605 differential pressure weekly
- Step 1 - Check: Loop isolated / under permit
- Step 2 - Action: Note the PDAH-5605 fouling alarm at 0.7 bar dP
- Step 2 - Check: Reference standard traceable
- Step 3 - Action: Correlate rising dP with any outlet-temperature shortfall
- Step 3 - Check: As-found & as-left recorded
- Step 4 - Action: Plan cleaning before the duty loss becomes critical
- Step 4 - Check: Trip / control action verified
- Step 5 - Action: Feed the trend into the exchanger cleaning program
- Step 5 - Check: Return to service confirmed

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Outlet temperature hunting around set-point | Likely Cause: Steam valve TV-5602 loop poorly tuned | Action: Retuned TIC-5602 PID, verified stable control
- Symptom: Erratic tube dP reading | Likely Cause: Impulse lines plugged with fines | Action: Cleaned and re-zeroed PDT-5605 transmitter
- Symptom: Cracked gauge glass on condensate pot | Likely Cause: Thermal/mechanical stress on glass | Action: Replaced LG-5606 gauge glass and seals

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: Trending the tube-side differential pressure predicts when cleaning is due before the duty is lost.
- Point 2: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-5601 before working on EA-5601.
- Point 3: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
